draft.shortGloss: to bring; to carry; to wear; to take
draft.emotion: helpful and ready, stepping forward with a load
notes: Covers both English 'bring' (towards the speaker or listener) and 'take' (away to another place).
Also commonly used for wearing clothes, glasses, or a hairstyle.

senses.definition: To take or carry something from one place to another.

examples.text: Devo portare questi documenti in ufficio.
examples.translation: I need to take these documents to the office.
examples.emotion: focused and determined, getting the task done

senses.definition: To have clothing, glasses, or accessories on your body.

examples.text: Oggi porto una giacca pesante perché fa freddo.
examples.translation: Today I am wearing a heavy jacket because it is cold.
examples.emotion: practical and comfortable, dressing for the weather

senses.definition: To accompany or drive someone to a place.

examples.text: Ti porto io alla stazione in macchina.
examples.translation: I'll drive you to the station.
examples.emotion: kind and obliging, offering a helpful favor

translations.from: Trasportare qualcosa da un luogo a un altro, tenendolo con sé.

translations.from: Avere indosso abiti, scarpe o accessori.
translations.to: Have clothing, shoes, or accessories on your body.

draftBefore.shortGloss: to carry; to wear; to lead

notes: Use portare when you are moving something from one place to another, whether in your hands or wearing it on your body.
Unlike English, Italian uses portare both for carrying things and for wearing clothes or accessories.
